name: Session not invalidated after logout
description:
Logging out does not end the session on the server. The logout response expires the session cookie in the browser, but the token itself remains valid: replaying it afterwards is still accepted as the user who logged out. Anyone who obtained the token earlier (from a shared or public computer, a proxy log, a cross-site scripting flaw or a stolen device) keeps the session even after the user has logged out, which defeats the point of logging out.

burpsy logged in, confirmed that the new token was accepted by a page that depends on the session, sent the token to the application's logout, saw the cookie expired, and replayed the same token read-only to the same page.

This row is burpsy's own: Burp's issue catalogue has no entry for it.
remediation: Destroy the server-side session at logout, so that the token is rejected from then on; for stateless tokens, keep a revocation list or a per-user token version until the token expires. Apply idle and absolute session timeouts as well. Clearing the cookie in the browser is not enough.

references.title: OWASP Session Management Cheat Sheet: Manual Session Expiration
OWASP WSTG-SESS-06: Testing for Logout Functionality
